page: Amazon Web Services c7g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance delivers 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, utilizing AWS Graviton3 processors based on the ARM Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture clocked at 2.6 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, 32 MB shared L3 cache, and hardware support for cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions. No local storage is attached to the instance, necessitating external block storage solutions such as Amazon EBS, and baseline network throughput is rated at 2 Gbps without provisioned GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier performance across general compute tasks. Synthetic testing shows mid-range results in multi-core processing with a stress-ng score of 6111.85 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4789.0, complemented by solid clang software compilation marks (6152.0). Data store operations also demonstrate balanced efficiency, clocking 6.65 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks alongside 8.02 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, workloads requiring heavy SIMD acceleration or large matrix operations show limitations due to the absence of AVX and AMX instruction sets. Extended instruction tests, ray tracing, and bzip3 decompression register in the bottom quartile, and large language model inference shows sluggish output (5.99 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model).

Given its compute-to-memory configuration and cost profile inherent to the Graviton processor line, the c7g.xlarge is suited for compiled microservices, web application backends, Redis caching layers, and continuous integration runners. Applications requiring dedicated CPU time without hyperthreading overhead benefit from this instance profile, provided the software stack supports the aarch64 architecture and does not rely on extensive x86 vector extensions or GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro platform, utilizing 64-bit ARM Neoverse-V1 Graviton3 processors running at 2.6 GHz. Configured with 4 dedicated physical vCPUs without hyperthreading and 8.0 GB of memory, it maintains a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance features 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, AES cryptographic hardware support, and lacks local disk storage, relying on external network volumes. Benchmark evaluations show solid average throughput in CPU stress testing, clang software compilation, static web serving, and Redis key-value workloads. Limitations appear in heavy SIMD vector operations, complex decompression, and machine learning inference tasks due to the lack of x86 vector extensions and dedicated accelerators. As an ARM-based compute resource, it serves software compilation, web serving tiers, and containerized microservices effectively.

8.0 GB system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU compute ratio)
